Answers to your questions are as follows:

A. Yes, trade it both ways. Why not? B. No, a flag is a big move in price followed by an "indecision" period. The FOs might take the form of RBDs/DBRs. I read a post from IF somewhere where he said that trading the edge of flags is easy money ( please take this as my interpretation and not the words out of IF's mouth).

Thanks for your replies Harry! For clarification though over your charts, does the FL have to be tested to make it the FL? Look at the charts below. The purple arrow is pointing to the FL. Would you call that the FL because of the support that was shown at the yellow arrows? In other words would have you tried and guessed that the level with the purple arrow was going to hold as a FL. Or is it like in chart two below?

ok, I just edited this to make sure my question was clear and just thought of this. My question is: You see price moving up and up. Along the way there are many RBR's. Any one of those could be the FL. So to tell which one will be the FL do you look to see which one sits above past resistance? Or do you wait for one of the RBR's to get pulled back to and tested? This way you will see which one will hold and that tells you the right FL. Then when price returns to that test (which will actually be the second return) that is your FTB? Make sense?

This chart shows my FL I marked from earlier. Was the FL that the yellow arrow is pointing to made by the previous supply from the blue arrow?
